product: commentary — no product. Reveals the comparison-ad landing page rule.
body: Roughly 99% of ecom brands run us-vs-them ads but send the click to their PDP with a comparison table buried below the fold. The rule: if the comparison is the angle, the comparison IS the landing page — a dedicated page with real data side by side, no trash talk, dressed as a listicle or advertorial, doing the one job the ad promised. Landing a comparison click on a PDP answers a question they didn't ask.
idea: The landing page must answer the exact question the ad asked — comparison ads need comparison pages.
sequencing: The audit finding (99% send to PDP).
The page spec (side-by-side, real data, no trash talk).
why_it_works: Click intent is specific — a comparison click landing on a PDP feels like a bait-and-switch.
what_to_steal: LC us-vs-them ads ("LC vs $12 Amazon necklace") must land on a dedicated comparison page, not the PDP.

product: commentary — no product. Us-vs-them comparison statics are in the "printing" list for 2026.
body: Dead in 2026: polished studio product videos, "hey guys" UGC intros, discount-led statics, founder story VSLs. Printing right now: ugly advertorial statics, long-form yapper ads, comment-reply UGC hooks, us-vs-them comparison statics. Caveat: the format is never the biggest lever — the angle underneath is.
idea: Us-vs-them statics are a printing format in 2026.
sequencing: Dead: polished studio product videos plus "hey guys" UGC intros.
Dead: discount-led statics plus founder story VSLs.
Printing: ugly advertorial statics plus long-form yapper ads.
Printing: comment-reply UGC hooks plus us-vs-them comparison statics.
Caveat: the angle underneath is the bigger lever.
why_it_works: Comparison gives "better" claims the context they need to mean something.
what_to_steal: Us-vs-them as a standing LC static cell.

product: A moisturizer built for the heat (brand unnamed) — four statics, one angle showcase.
body: Four static executions of a single angle for a heat-proof moisturizer: before & after, feature callout, headline callout, us vs them. Four photos attached.
idea: One angle, four static wrappers — format diversification without new angles.
why_it_works: Same angle in four formats finds which wrapper the audience prefers — cheap testing.
what_to_steal: The "1 angle × 4 statics" test for LC: the tarnish-proof angle as before/after, feature callout, headline callout, and us-vs-them.

product: commentary — no product. A static ad designer's portfolio pitch (callout, us-vs-them, DTC, UGC).
body: A designer pitches static ad services: every product has a different story and creative challenge; specialties include callout, us-vs-them, DTC, and UGC statics; open for projects via DM. Photo attached.
idea: Static design as a service, with us-vs-them as a core offering.
sequencing: Every product brings a different story and creative challenge.
why_it_works: Specialists sell the format menu — us-vs-them is standard enough to be a line item.
what_to_steal: Nothing creative — but confirms us-vs-them is a commoditized, hireable skill for LC.

product: commentary — no product. An agency's us-vs-them philosophy (1,000+ statics/month, ~10% us-vs-them).
hook: "We make 1,000+ statics every month. Around 10% are Us vs Them."
body: Showing the difference beats talking about the product. "Better quality," "better results," and "better value" mean nothing without context — us-vs-them supplies it. Compare against the old way, a common alternative, a generic option, or even the problem itself. Compare ONE thing that matters — price, ingredients, time, results, quality, convenience — then make that difference obvious in the creative. Four photos attached.
idea: One difference, made obvious — comparison ads work when they isolate a single meaningful axis.
why_it_works: Single-axis comparison is instantly parseable — the brain gets the verdict in one glance.
what_to_steal: The one-thing rule for LC: each us-vs-them static compares ONE axis (tarnish test, price-per-wear, skin safety).

product: commentary — no product. A list of printing static formats, led by us-vs-them.
body: Twenty-two printing static formats listed, led by us-vs-them: whiteboard, breaking news, doodle, low stock alert, iPhone notes, transformation, Google search, bundle, "zero stars", "we are sorry", Reddit, IG message, IG story, claymation, email screenshot, tweet screenshot, native ads, "don't buy this", green screen, memes, text on palm.
idea: Us-vs-them leads a broad menu of printing static formats.
sequencing: Us vs them leads the list.
Whiteboard, breaking news, doodle, low stock alert.
iPhone notes, transformation, Google search, bundle.
Reddit, tweet screenshot, native ads, memes, text on palm — plus more.
why_it_works: Menus beat single recommendations — brands can pick what fits.
what_to_steal: The menu as LC's static testing backlog; us-vs-them stays at the top.

product: commentary — no product. Top-5 dropshipping formats ranked; us-vs-them comparison is #3.
hook: "the 5 ad creative formats that convert highest in dropshipping right now ranked by performance."
body: #1 UGC problem/solution (friend-recommendation feel; unpolished converts). #2 "TikTok made me buy it" (fast cuts, social proof built in). #3 us-vs-them comparison — split screen, your product vs "the other brand," exaggerated: yours works perfectly, theirs falls apart (truncated). #4 founder talking head; #5 text-overlay slideshow (per gist).
idea: Exaggerated split-screen comparison is the #3 converter in dropshipping.
sequencing: Founder talking head; text-overlay slideshow (per gist).
why_it_works: Exaggeration makes the verdict unmissable — the visual does the arguing.
what_to_steal: The exaggerated split screen for LC: LC piece vs competitor piece in water/sweat — one shines, one fades.

product: commentary — no product. The us-vs-copycat playbook: iPhone screen scrolling fake Amazon listings.
hook: "launch ads ASAP calling out copycats and replicas."
body: One of the highest-CVR middle-of-funnel creatives: an iPhone screen scrolling through fake Amazon listings while narrating the difference between the real product and replicas; then tailor the PDP with "original/only" details and replica warnings. Positioned as an easy, needed lift going into Q4. Quoted post: "Drop this image inside your PDP carousel and watch CVR go up."
idea: Name-and-shame the copycats on screen — the scroll through fakes is the proof.
sequencing: iPhone screen scrolls fake Amazon listings.
Narrator explains real vs replica differences.
why_it_works: Showing the fakes on Amazon makes the threat concrete; the brand becomes the safe choice.
what_to_steal: Directly LC-relevant — LC has copycat problems: iPhone scroll through fake LC listings on Amazon, narrating the tells (no PVD, turns skin green), plus a PDP badge as "the original waterproof jewelry."
